# Universe24

> One line of whole-number arithmetic on a cubic lattice of Node-clocks, Rule3 in the law's flux form, read through clicks: the formulas it shares with nature and adds. A paper archived on Zenodo and at the tag v1.1.0, its supplement with every proof, the law of the lattice, the derivations as scripts, the engine, Tensor24 (src/tensor24/), with its tests and the paper's engine at the tag v1.1.0, and one world, Universe24: three files of whole numbers (examples/tensor24/), every Node-clock stepping by one act, the record read through the clicks by one decoder. The old engine left the working tree on 2026-10-30 and stands in git's history. Author: Alon Gonen, independent researcher, Haifa, Israel (ORCID 0009-0008-2701-4599). Licence MIT. Permanent record: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23466436 (the concept DOI of the releases from 3.0.0 on, resolving to the latest version; the versions 1.1.0 to 2.1.0 under https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23190113); the current software version, 4.0.0, Universe24: one Node, one universe, under the concept DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23466436 (no release is tagged for 4.0.0 by the owner's word of 2026-10-24, 23:5x UTC; the version number stands in the files, the concept DOI resolves to the latest Zenodo deposit (3.0.0)); 3.0.0: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23466437

## In plain words

Suppose nature is discrete: space is made of Node-clocks, and between one Node-clock and the next nothing moves faster than light. A cubic centimetre then holds an astronomical number of Node-clocks, so no centre can know and decide for all of them; each Node-clock acts on its own, by a rule of its own, seeing only itself and its six neighbours. Universe24 is that rule: one line of whole-number arithmetic with no free number but the universe's three integers, den, the full rate and the whole piece's action. A Node-clock holds, for every train of the universe, its notch now, its notch one tick before, and a remainder; at every tick it forms one sum, twice its notch now less its notch before at the teeth count, plus what crosses its six Meshes at each Mesh's reach, less its own mass term, zero for light, plus the carried remainder, and divides by the teeth count; the quotient is its next notch and the new remainder is kept. Nothing is lost, so the rule is exactly reversible. The rule is on whole numbers of any size and carries no bound; the width of the integers is a key of the universe file and no bound stands in the engine's code (docs/ALGEBRA.md, line 100). The tick is the count of rounds and no Node-clock reads it. The trains are derived from den: light, the holder of the volume and the holder of the sign, and one plane train per point of den's circle; the reach of a Mesh comes from the train's pair, the Node-clock's rates and the Mesh's tension, a mass is no input of a file, a gear's mass being its own rest beat, read in the clicks (docs/ALGEBRA.md, decisions 35 and 37). A world that declares nothing is seeded with light at one quantum on every Node-clock of the torus, and the great clock reads itself: where two whole quanta stand at a Node-clock a pair of matter is born there, the Node-clock's own read of itself and its six Meshes, two kinds of click and no third, the whole click with nothing to choose and the split click drawing by its parts' sizes, the one place a choice enters (docs/ALGEBRA.md, line 156); the hole is the exact take, and a refusal is a logged line. A Node-clock does not know trains; they come out through the click, and one reckoner names them from the clicks. The click is the one act with a direction; every other act is a bijection, and the top of a Node-clock's own time gear needs no act (the turnover is cancelled, decision 27); what the great clock shows of a return is read from the chart's clicks and named (docs/FURTHER_RESEARCH.md, first). The paper's one claim: the rule helps compute things in nature. Every number in the paper is reproduced by a script in the repository.

## Read first

- [The paper, 40 pages](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/papers/one_rule/Universe24_Paper.pdf): "Universe24: one simple rule, the formulas it shares with nature and adds" (Alon Gonen, 2026)
- [The supplement, Online Resource 1, 85 pages](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/papers/one_rule/Universe24_Supplement.pdf): the claims list and the algebraic steps of every derivation
- [The time paper, 22 pages](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/papers/spacetime_events/Universe24_Discrete_Spacetime_of_Events_Paper.pdf): "A discrete spacetime of events in whole numbers: why clocks slow, why nothing outruns light, and why time has a direction only where something was measured" (Alon Gonen, 2026), its source, run and checks in papers/spacetime_events/, built and run by its build.sh
- [README](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/README.md): the aim, what stands (Tensor24, the old engine out), the law in four lines, the description of the system, how to run it, the documents, the papers
- [The architecture](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the one document that tells the system and the one the work runs from: the parts, the Node-clock first (the three files, the loader, the Node-clock, the runner, the record, the decoder, the visualizer, the guards), each told by the clock, the board and the clicks, with its algebra, home, test and status, and who may import whom

## The documents

- [The law of the lattice](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/docs/ALGEBRA.md): the project's seven postulates at its head in one place (the many Node-clocks with no centre and the locality they force; whole numbers for the reversibility of time; the speed of light at most; nature cyclic and no information lost; the Node-clock with no if; rates multiplying along a gear train, so the time gear's law linear in the logarithm of the rate; the board progressing in complexity with time, as a general idea), then one algebraic line per rule, a changed line holding its new wording alone and the former clauses standing by name in its closing section, the one Node-clock, the click's read of the great clock, the great clock reading itself, the trains at the click, the volume holder, and the turnover (cancelled, decision 27)
- [Contributing](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/CONTRIBUTING.md): forks and pull requests, the ground rules, the checks, how to report an error or a failed reproduction
- [What changed](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/CHANGELOG.md): what changed since the new engine, Tensor24; the earlier history stands in git

## The code

- [Repository on GitHub](https://github.com/Closer24/Universe24): the derivations as scripts (tools/derivations/), the implementation (src/tensor24/), the tests that prove the Node-clock's law (tests/), the one world's three files (examples/tensor24/), and the tools that check, run and decode it (tools/tensor24_files.py, tensor24_run.py, tensor24_decode.py)
- [Zenodo record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23466436): the concept DOI of the releases from 3.0.0 on, the permanent record and the one to cite, resolving to the latest version (the versions 1.1.0 to 2.1.0 under [10.5281/zenodo.23190113](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23190113)); the current software version, 4.0.0, Universe24: one Node-clock, one universe, stands under the concept DOI with no version record (no release is tagged for 4.0.0 by the owner's word of 2026-10-24, 23:5x UTC; the version number stands in the files, the concept DOI resolves to the latest Zenodo deposit (3.0.0)); 3.0.0, the click as one act, the spin and the atom, is [10.5281/zenodo.23466437](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23466437); the paper's engine, version 1.1.0, is 10.5281/zenodo.23202100
